title: Bloch's Law for Finite-Range Heisenberg Ferromagnets in Three Dimensions
main_claim: Fix spin S and a nonnegative, symmetric, finite-range coupling J whose support generates Z^3. Then lim_{beta->inf} beta^{3/2}(S - m_{S,J}(beta)) = zeta(3/2)/(8 pi^{3/2} sqrt(det D_{S,J})), where D_{S,J} = (S/2) sum_z J(z) z z^T. The magnetization m is the right h-derivative at 0 of the infinite-volume pressure. The order of limits is: volume first, then h down to 0, then beta to infinity.
coverage:
I read all seven sections in full and checked the following.
- Sec 2: the constants in the loop representation (slot-edge rate J/2, the shift e^{beta w/4}). The singleton pin identity d = r/(1+r), re-derived independently. The simultaneous pin bound via stable polynomials and AM-GM. The exposure disintegration and the next-pin Schur-complement kernel; I checked their logic, but they are imported from the Ordering companion.
- Sec 3: the Nash inequality with exponents 10/3 and 4/3 and its averaging proof. The flow-overlap exponent q = 2k-3. The sparse-source energy annulus sum. The spread-source energy: the near part via Young with ||kappa_s||_1 ~ s, the far part sum ~ tau^{-1/2} + R^{-0.98}.
- Sec 4: the blocking lemma (cases by grid time / marks). Sparsity of the witness tree (needs b^alpha > 4) and its counting. delta_R = O_K(beta^{-12/5}). Localization with the constant a independent of K. The Nash time count in the diffusion proposition (regular time >= 0.67 b'). The hitting-energy algebra and the suffix-energy identity E_y - (1/2)(||y||^2 - ||U*y||^2) = (1/2)||y - U*y||^2. The downward induction: P = E ∪ T is a strict grid superset, and r = O(beta^{-0.99}) = o(p).
- Sec 5: the finite return expansion algebra. The telescoping A_Q v = Q eta - Q^K eta gives exactly a_1 + ... + a_{2K-1}. In the long-tail completing-square bound the constant 3 C_sp K^{-1/2} beta^{-3/2} does not depend on K. The K=1 corollary uses no later results, so there is no circularity.
- Sec 6: the ideal heat-kernel constant kappa = (4 pi)^{-3/2} det^{-1/2}. Slot uniformity after a seam gives the exact factor ell^{-1}. The midpoint pairing reduction. The encounter bound O_K(beta^{-1/2} log^3 beta), which uses the corollary's density bound. The Bonferroni lower bound with fresh-walk factorization. The r-vs-d correction is O(beta^{-3}).
- Sec 7: the boundary pressure equivalence (insertion factor 4). The field-as-pin-mixture identity, (1-b)^{D_down} = e^{-beta h D_down}. The integration in h and the order of limits. The final coefficient kappa zeta(3/2) = zeta(3/2)/(8 pi^{3/2} sqrt det D); it agrees with the standard nearest-neighbor Bloch constant.
Not re-derived: the Ordering companion's deterministic geometry (local connectivity rho(3,b), routed hull flows with envelope k = 2 - 3 nu, Prop 6.2). The paper states that input precisely and applies it per coset.
sibling_notes: The two family-271 siblings (rank345 spontaneous magnetization, rank372 spherical law) both returned no_gap_found. This paper reuses the same Ordering-companion machinery: the exposure disintegration, the exterior-moment / next-pin determinant identity, sparse-witness blocking tails and routed flows. rank345 says it numerically verified the E[Sigma|G] Schur kernel, so I did not re-verify it. What is new here is the coset reduction for finite-range J, the K-independent long-return remainder, and the midpoint coupling to the full-dispersion ideal walk. All three check out.
